title: COMP/70/1999 of In The Matter Of Techinvest India Pvt Ltd, Vs In The Matter Of Assam Power and Electrical Ltd,

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Company Petition No. 70 of 1999
(New Number 10 of 2003)
M/s Assam Power & Electrical Ltd. .....Petitioner
 Versus
Techinvest India (P) Ltd. ....Respondent
Mr. Parikshit Saini, Advocate for M/s Assam Power & Electrical Ltd.
Mr. Pankaj Kumar Singh and Mr. Vinay Kumar, Advocates for major shareholder,
namely, Mr. Rajiv Gosain.
Mr. Anil Kumar Joshi, Advocate for Official Liquidator.
Mr. B.M. Pingal, Advocate for Mr. P.K. Seth (one of the secured creditor).
Mr. P.R. Mullick, Advocate for Auction Purchaser.
with
Company Appeal No. 2 of 2012
State Bank of India and another. ......Appellants
 Versus
M/s Tech Invest Private Ltd. .....Respondent
There is no representation for the appellants.
Mr. Pankaj Kumar Singh and Mr. Vinay Kumar, Advocates for the respondent.
Mr. Anil Kumar Joshi, Advocate for Official Liquidator.
Dated: 30th December, 2020
Hon'ble Manoj K. Tiwari, J.
 Misc. Application (I.A. No. 9649 of 2019) has been
filed by M/s Assam Power & Electrical Ltd. (renamed as SAM
Global Securities Ltd.), which is an unsecured creditor of
M/s Techinvest India Private Ltd. (company under
liquidation).
2. By means of this Misc. Application, M/s Assam
Power & Electrical Ltd. has sought transfer of Company
Petition No. 10 of 2003 to National Company Law Tribunal
under Section 434 of the Companies Act, 2013 and
Companies (Transfer of Pending Proceedings), Rules, 2016.

2
3. Section 434 (1) (c) of the Companies Act, 2013
reads as under:
"434. Transfer of certain pending proceedings.-
(1) On such date as may be notified by the Central
Government in this behalf,-
(a) .............
(b) ............
(c) all proceedings under the Companies Act,
1956, including proceedings relating to
arbitration, compromise, arrangements and
reconstruction and winding up of companies,
pending immediately before such date before
any District Court or High Court, shall stand
transferred to the Tribunal and the Tribunal
may proceed to deal with such proceedings
from the stage before their transfer:
Provided that only such proceedings relating
to the winding up of companies shall be
transferred to the Tribunal that are at a stage
as may be prescribed by the Central
Government.
[Provided further that only such proceedings
relating to cases other than winding-up, for
which orders for allowing or otherwise of the
proceedings are not reserved by the High
Courts shall be transferred to the Tribunal:
[Provided further that -]
(i) all proceedings under the Companies
Act, 1956 other than the cases relating
to winding up of companies that are
reserved for orders for allowing or
otherwise such proceedings; or
(ii) the proceedings relating to winding
up of companies which have not been
transferred from the High Courts; shall
be dealt with in accordance with
provisions of the Companies Act, 1956
and the Companies (Court) Rules,
1959:]
[Provided also that proceedings relating to
cases of voluntary winding up of a company
where notice of the resolution by
advertisement has been given under sub-section (1) of section 485 of the Companies
Act, 1956 but the company has not been
dissolved before the 1st April, 2017 shall
continue to be dealt with in accordance with
provisions of the Companies Act. 1956 and
the Companies (Court) Rules, 1959:]

3
[Provided further that any party or parties to
any proceedings relating to the winding up of
companies pending before any Court
immediately before the commencement of the
Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code
(Amendment) Ordinance, 2018, may file an
application for transfer of such proceedings
and the Court may by order transfer such
proceedings to the Tribunal and the
proceedings so transferred shall be dealt with
by the Tribunal as an application for initiation
of corporate insolvency resolution process
under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code,
2016 (31 of 2016).]"

4. A plain reading of fifth proviso to Section 434 (1)
(c) reveals that any party to a proceeding relating to winding
up of a company pending before any Court immediately
before commencement of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy
Code (Amendment) Ordinance, 2018, may file an application
for transfer of such proceedings and the Court may by order
transfer such proceedings to the Tribunal and the
proceedings so transferred shall be dealt with by the
Tribunal as an application for initiation of corporate
insolvency resolution process under the Insolvency and
Bankruptcy Code, 2016.
5. Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of M/s
Kaledonia Jute and Fibres Pvt. Ltd. Vs. M/s Axis Nirman
and Industries Ltd. & others, reported in (2020) SCC Online
SC 943, has held as under:
"47. Therefore, we are of the considered
view that the petitioner-herein will
come within the definition of the
expression "party" appearing in the
5th proviso to Clause (c) of Sub-section
(1) of Section 434 of the Companies Act,
2013 and that the petitioner is entitled
to seek a transfer of the pending
winding up proceedings against the
first respondent, to the NCLT. It is

4
important to note that the restriction
under Rules 5 and 6 of the Companies
(Transfer of Pending Proceedings)
Rules, 2016 relating to the stage at
which a transfer could be ordered, has
no application to the case of a transfer
covered by the 5th proviso to clause (c)
of sub-section (1) of Section 434.
Therefore, the impugned order of the
High court rejecting the petition for
transfer on the basis of Rule 26 of the
Companies (Court) Rules, 1959 is
flawed."
6. The view taken in the case of M/s Kaledonia Jute
and Fibres Pvt. Ltd. (Supra) has been reiterated by Hon'ble
Supreme Court in a subsequent judgment rendered in the
case of Action Ispat and Power Pvt. Ltd. Vs. Shyam Metalics
and Energy Ltd., reported in (2020) SCC Online SC 1025.
Relevant extract of paragraph no. 31 of the said judgment is
reproduced below:
"31. .............................................. So long
as no actual sales of the immovable or
movable properties have taken place, nothing
irreversible is done which would warrant a
Company Court staying its hands on a
transfer application made to it by a creditor or
any party to the proceedings. It is only where
the winding up proceedings have reached a
stage where it would be irreversible, making it
impossible to set the clock back that the
Company Court must proceed with the
winding up, instead of transferring the
proceedings to the NCLT to now be decided in
accordance with the provisions of the Code.
Whether this stage is reached would depend
upon the facts and circumstances of each
case."
7. Admittedly, in the present case, Hon'ble
Allahabad High Court passed an order of winding up in
respect of M/s Techinvest India Private Ltd. on 12.07.2000
and, subsequently, assets of M/s Techinvest Private Ltd.
were sold in favour of M/s Texplas India Private Ltd. in an

5
auction and auction sale was confirmed by this Court.
However, the auction as well as confirmation of sale in
favour of M/s Texplas India Private Ltd. was set aside by
Hon'ble Supreme Court vide judgment dated 11.08.2015
rendered in Civil Appeal No. 6055-6056 of 2015. Thereafter,
this Court, on 04.03.2020, passed the following order:
"Mr. Parikshit Saini, learned counsel
appearing for M/s Assam Power &
Electrical Ltd. (petitioner herein) submits
that Hon'ble Supreme Court vide judgment
dated 11.08.2015 passed in Civil Appeal
Nos. 6055-6056 of 2015 had directed the
Official Liquidator to forthwith recover
possession of the properties and proceed
with a fresh auction after obtaining fresh
valuation report and fixing the reserve bid.
He further submits that auction
purchaser, namely, M/s Texples India (P)
Ltd. has not handed-over physical
possession of the assets of the Company
(M/s Assam Power & Electrical Ltd.) under
liquidation, despite the order passed by
Hon'ble Supreme Court.
In such view of the matter, Official
Liquidator is directed to take physical
possession of the property in terms of
order passed by Hon'ble Supreme Court,
within 15 days from today.
Senior Superintendent of Police, Haridwar
is directed to provide adequate police force
to facilitate taking over the physical
possession of the property, by the Official
Liquidator.
The Official Liquidator shall secure the
assets of the Company in liquidation so
that the same is preserved. Compliance
report shall be filed by Official Liquidator
by the next date of listing.
List this matter on 15.04.2020."
8. The order dated 04.03.2020 was challenged by
M/s Texplas India Private Ltd. by filing Special Appeal No.
01 of 2020, which was dismissed by Division Bench of this
Court on 09.06.2020. M/s Texplas India Private Ltd.,

6
thereafter, filed S.L.P. No. 7530 of 2020 and the said S.L.P.
was dismissed vide order dated 16.06.2020. Order passed
by Hon'ble Supreme Court in S.L.P. No. 7530 of 2020 is
reproduced below:
"We found no ground to interfere with the
impugned order passed by the High Court.
The Special Leave Petition is, accordingly,
dismissed.
However, it is open to the petitioner to pursue
the application for refund in accordance with
law. Let the order be complied with and
report be submitted to this Court within one
month."
9. Mr. P.R. Mullick, learned counsel appearing for
M/s Texplas India Private Ltd. has opposed the misc.
application seeking transfer of proceedings to National
Company Law Tribunal on the ground that the assets of
Techinvest India (P) Ltd. were purchased by his client in an
auction, therefore, these proceedings have reached the stage
of irreversibility, thus, proceedings cannot be transferred.
10. This Court is not impressed with the submission
advanced by Mr. P.R. Mullick, learned counsel appearing for
M/s Texplas India Private Ltd. Hon'ble Supreme Court in
Civil Appeal No. 6055-6056 of 2015 had been pleased to set
aside the sale of assets of the company under liquidation, in
favour of M/s Texplas India Private Ltd. and it was provided
that Official Liquidator shall forthwith recover possession of
assets from M/s Texplas India Private Ltd. Thus, it is the
official liquidator, who is having legal possession over the
assets of the company under liquidation, therefore, it cannot
be said that point of no return has been reached in these
proceedings.

7
11. Mr. Pankaj Kumar Singh, learned counsel
appearing for major shareholder, namely, Mr. Rajiv Gosain,
who is supporting the misc. application, submits that
Punjab National Bank, which had granted a term loan of
` 5.6 Crores to M/s Texplas India Private Ltd., was also a
party before Hon'ble Supreme Court in Civil Appeal Nos.
6055-6056 of 2015.
12. Mr. B.M. Pingal, learned counsel appearing for
Mr. P.K. Seth (one of the secured creditor) also supports
transfer of Company Petition No. 10 of 2003 to National
Company Law Tribunal.
13. Mr. Anil Joshi, learned counsel appearing for
Official Liquidator, submits that, in view of the judgment
rendered by Hon'ble Supreme Court in Action Ispat and
Power Pvt. Ltd. (Supra), he is not in a position to oppose the
misc. application seeking transfer of proceedings.
14. For the aforesaid facts and reasons, the Misc.
Application is allowed. Company Petition No. 10 of 2003 as
well as Company Appeal No.2 of 2012 filed under Rule 164
of Companies (Court) Rules, 1959 are transferred to National
Company Law Tribunal, Allahabad Bench, for
determination, in accordance with law.
15. Registry is directed to send the entire records to
National Company Law Tribunal, Allahabad Bench, within a
week. Parties shall appear before learned Tribunal on
05.02.2021, without any further notice.

8
16. In view of the long pendency of the Company
Petition, learned Tribunal is requested to dispose of the
matter as expeditiously as possible, preferably within a
period of nine months from the date of appearance.
 (Manoj K. Tiwari, J.)
 30.12.2020
Arpan
